| Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI), Belfast | Church registers, estate papers, valuation records, militia records, probate, court records for County Antrim | In-person; eCatalogue online at www.nidirect.gov.uk/proni |
| General Register Office Northern Ireland (GRONI), Belfast | Civil birth, death, and marriage registers from 1845/1864 | In-person; online index at GRONI website; certificates by fee |
| The National Archives (Kew, UK) | British Army service and pension records; Admiralty records | In-person; some records online at Ancestry and FindMyPast |
| National Archives of Ireland (Dublin) | Pre-1922 centralized records; some County Antrim wills and probate abstracts; Tithe books | In-person; some collections online |
| Registry of Deeds (Dublin) | Land transaction records from 1708 | In-person; some indexes online |

## Records NOT online

- Estate papers at PRONI (tenant lists, rent rolls, leases for Billy parish townlands) — physical access at PRONI only
- Kirk session minutes for Presbyterian congregations in Billy parish — at PRONI or individual congregations
- Original civil registration certificates (indexes are online; full certificates require a fee application to GRONI)
- British Army service records for the period 1780–1850 at The National Archives, Kew — partially online via Ancestry/FindMyPast subscription
- Vestry records for Church of Ireland in Billy parish — at PRONI

## Known record losses

- **1922 fire:** The Public Record Office of Ireland in Dublin was destroyed in June 1922 during the Civil War. This destroyed the majority of Church of Ireland parish registers that had been centrally deposited there, many pre-1858 original wills, and the 1821 and 1831 census returns for all of Ireland. County Antrim records held separately at what became PRONI in Belfast were largely not affected by the 1922 fire
- **1861 and 1871 census returns for Ireland:** Officially destroyed by order of the Irish government; no returns survive
- **Many 1821 and 1831 census returns:** Largely destroyed in 1922; surviving fragments are at the National Archives of Ireland

## Research tips

- **Naming conventions (from FamilySearch Wiki, Ireland Naming Customs page, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Naming_Customs):** A traditional naming pattern was widely used in Ireland through the later 19th century. The first son was usually named for the father's father; the second son for the mother's father; the third son for the father himself; the fourth son for the father's eldest brother. The first daughter was usually named for the mother's mother; the second daughter for the father's mother; the third daughter for the mother. This pattern is a clue to grandparents' given names, not a rule — it was not universally followed, and a broken pattern is not evidence that two people with the same name are different individuals
- **Surname variation (from FamilySearch Wiki, Ireland Naming Customs page):** Irish Gaelic surnames with the prefixes Mac and O were frequently dropped or restored across generations and even within a single family. The same family may appear as O'Flynn, Flynn, and Flinn in different records. Search all spelling variants, and do not treat the presence or absence of the prefix as distinguishing two individuals
- **Search the townland, not just the civil parish:** Billy civil parish contains numerous townlands. Knowing the specific townland where a family lived is essential for locating them in Griffith's Valuation, estate papers, and church records. The Ordnance Survey Memoirs of Ireland (compiled 1830s) describe County Antrim townlands in detail and are available at PRONI and in published form
- **Estate papers may predate other records:** For the period 1780–1823 (before the Tithe Applotment Books begin), landlord estate records at PRONI may be the only source that places a named family in a specific townland. Identify which estate covered the townlands of Billy parish and search those estate papers at PRONI
- **Presbyterian versus Church of Ireland registers:** The religious composition of Billy parish is mixed, but Presbyterian registers in north Antrim often survive further back than Church of Ireland registers (many of which were destroyed in 1922). Do not search only one denomination — a family may have crossed denominational lines for a marriage, or the surviving register for one congregation may cover members of another that lacked a local minister at that date
- **FamilySearch Wiki unreachable during this survey (Ireland Vital Records, Ireland Genealogy, Ireland Church Records, Ireland Land and Property, County Antrim Genealogy, all four wiki_place_page sections); these pages may exist — re-run locality-guide before relying on their absence.**

# Locality Guide: Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania (1840–1880)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** 1811 (from place_search, dateRange +1811/)
- **County seat / administrative center:** Not confirmed by tool results during this survey
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Pennsylvania, United States
- **Population during period:** Population data was not returned by the survey tools
- **Economy:** Not confirmed by tool results
- **Ethnic composition:** Not confirmed by tool results
- **Religious denominations:** Church records in English and German survive (1842–1895), indicating German-speaking congregations alongside English-speaking ones
- **Key historical events:** Not confirmed by tool results

> Note: The FamilySearch Wiki returned only generic content (at https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Genealogy_Research_Guide) for every Pennsylvania and Schuylkill-specific page requested during this survey. No jurisdiction-specific facts were drawn from those pages. Where a wiki page is cited below, it is the generic fallback page, not a Pennsylvania-specific article.

## Boundary changes
- Schuylkill County was formed in 1811; boundaries during the 1840–1880 target period are not further described by the tools consulted.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** The Pennsylvania Vital Records wiki page returned only generic content — no jurisdiction-specific registration start date at any level (town, county, or statewide) was established. The generic page states that many U.S. states did not require statewide registration until the early 1900s. Do not assume civil vital records exist for Schuylkill County for births and deaths during 1840–1880.
- **What exists:** No indexed birth or death collection for Schuylkill County was returned. Marriage records are represented by one digitized image volume (image group 007936753), covering 1870–1910, with 94 images, **browse-only** (0% name-indexed, not full-text searchable).
- **Where held:** The marriage volume is on FamilySearch (image group 007936753); browsed image by image with no search interface.
- **Gaps:** No birth or death record volume for the target period was found. No pre-1870 marriage volume was returned.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church records (see below); census mortality schedules (1850–1885); cemetery records.

### Church records
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials, confirmations
- **What exists (volumes):** One digitized image volume (image group 007936751) covers Schuylkill County Church Records, 1842–1895, with 187 images in English and German. **Browse-only** (0% name-indexed, not full-text searchable) — must be browsed image by image with no search interface.
- **Collections:** A collection titled "Pennsylvania, Schuylkill County Church Records (synthetic test fixture)" (collection SYNTH-PA-CHURCH, 1708–1985) appeared in collections_search with 982,415 person records. Its own title includes the label "synthetic test fixture"; treat this result as unverified until confirmed at https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/SYNTH-PA-CHURCH.
- **Language:** English and German; 19th-century German script required for German entries.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch holds the digitized image volume (007936751).
- **Gaps:** Denominations and parishes covered by the volume are not identified in the tool results.

### Census records
- **Federal census:** Decennial federal censuses (1840, 1850, 1860, 1870, 1880) cover Schuylkill County. The 1850 Schuylkill County census is indexed on Ancestry (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1276/). Mortality schedules (listing deaths in the year preceding the census) were produced from 1850 through 1880 and cover this county.
- **State census:** No Pennsylvania state census existed during 1840–1880 (the wiki returned only generic content and confirmed no state enumerations).
- **Access:** The 1850 Schuylkill census on Ancestry is name-indexed (subscription). FamilySearch holds federal census images for all years; indexing status should be verified at FamilySearch directly.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, estate inventories, letters of administration, guardianship files
- **What exists:** One digitized image volume (image group 007936749) covers Schuylkill County Probate Records, 1851–1930, with 412 images. **Browse-only** (0% indexed, not full-text searchable). Additionally, collection 1999196 ("Pennsylvania, Probate Records, 1683–1994") holds 3,200,560 state-level images; 0 records are indexed — browse-only.
- **Where held:** Originals at the county courthouse. FamilySearch holds digitized image volumes (007936749; collection 1999196).
- **Gaps:** No probate volume before 1851 appeared for this county.

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Metes-and-bounds (Pennsylvania)
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** The Pennsylvania Land and Property wiki page returned only generic content; it notes county courthouses hold deed books.
- **What exists:** One digitized image volume (image group 007936752) covers Schuylkill County Deed Records, 1815–1900, with 543 images. **22% name-indexed** — a portion is searchable, but 78% must be browsed image by image.
- **Where held:** Originals at the county courthouse. FamilySearch holds the digitized volume (007936752).

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Mexican-American War (1846–1848); Civil War (1861–1865)
- **Record types:** Service records, pension files, bounty land warrants; Civil War draft records
- **Where held:** NARA holds federal military service and pension records. The generic wiki page confirms this; no Schuylkill-specific military collection was returned by the survey tools.

### Cemetery records
- **Online coverage:** No cemetery-specific collection for Schuylkill County appeared in the survey tools. The curated external links did not include FindAGrave or BillionGraves for this county.
- **Physical records:** Sexton records and burial registers are held by individual cemeteries and churches; the county historical society may hold transcriptions.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** No newspaper titles or dates for Schuylkill County were returned by the survey tools.
- **Where held:** Pennsylvania State Archives and historical libraries hold Pennsylvania newspapers on microfilm. Online access through Newspapers.com and similar services should be checked directly.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Record types:** Passenger arrival manifests; declarations of intention and petitions for naturalization (court-generated); border crossing records
- **Naturalization:** One digitized image volume (image group 007936750) covers Schuylkill County Naturalization Records, 1849–1915, with 298 images. **Browse-only** (0% indexed, not full-text searchable). Prior to September 1906, any court of record could grant citizenship — declarations and petitions may also appear in state and federal court files.
- **Passenger lists:** Held at NARA. The nearest major port for 1840–1880 arrivals was Philadelphia, PA. NARA and Ancestry hold indexed manifests.
- **Content note:** Passenger arrival manifests list all persons aboard, including infants and young children traveling with parents. Examine the full manifest when researching a family.

### Tax records
- **What exists:** Ancestry holds "Pennsylvania, U.S., Tax and Exoneration Lists, 1768–1801" (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/7667/), which predates the 1840–1880 target period. No tax record collection for the target period was returned.
- **Where held:** County tax records for 1840–1880 are likely at the county courthouse or Pennsylvania State Archives but no digitized version was returned.
- **Substitute value:** Tax lists substitute for missing census years; county tax rolls name heads of household and taxable persons annually.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Pennsylvania, Probate Records, 1683–1994 (collection 1999196); Deed Records 1815–1900 (image group 007936752); Naturalization Records 1849–1915 (image group 007936750); Church Records 1842–1895 (image group 007936751); Marriage Records 1870–1910 (image group 007936753) | Probate, land, naturalization, church, and marriage records not in other online collections | Free |
| Ancestry | 1850 United States Federal Census – Schuylkill County (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1276/) | Indexed 1850 census — no equivalent indexed collection found on FamilySearch | Subscription |

**Coverage of this survey:** 5 digitized volumes match this place and period; the returned set is complete (complete: true from volume_search). One collections_search result is flagged in its own title as a synthetic test fixture and should be verified before use.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Schuylkill County Courthouse | Deeds, probate, court and naturalization originals | In-person / mail |
| Pennsylvania State Archives | State-level records; some county records; military | In-person / online request |
| County historical or genealogical society | Transcriptions, newspapers, local histories | In-person / contact society |
| National Archives (NARA) | Federal census, military service and pension, passenger lists | In-person / online (Ancestry / FamilySearch) |

## Records NOT online
- Birth and death records for 1840–1880: no indexed collection or digitized image volume appeared.
- Tax records for 1840–1880: not found in any digitized collection.
- Cemetery / sexton records: not in any returned collection.
- Local newspapers from the period: not in any returned online database.
- Approximately 78% of the Deed Records volume (image group 007936752) is not name-indexed and must be browsed image by image.
- Church records (007936751), marriage records (007936753), naturalization records (007936750), and probate records (007936749) are all browse-only with no name index.

## Known record losses
No tool result in this survey stated that any specific Schuylkill County record set was destroyed or lost. An absence from the survey results is a coverage gap, not confirmed loss. Consult the county courthouse and Pennsylvania State Archives directly to determine the survival and custody of any record class not found online.

## Research tips
- The FamilySearch Wiki returned only generic content for all Pennsylvania and Schuylkill-specific pages requested (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Genealogy_Research_Guide). Consult the Pennsylvania Genealogy article at familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pennsylvania_Genealogy and the Schuylkill County article at familysearch.org/en/wiki/Schuylkill_County,_Pennsylvania_Genealogy directly — those pages may carry jurisdiction-specific guidance not retrieved here.
- Because Pennsylvania did not require statewide civil registration of births and deaths until after 1880, church records are the primary vital-events source for 1840–1880. The Church Records volume (image group 007936751, 1842–1895) covers this period but must be browsed image by image, and German-language entries require reading 19th-century German script.
- Pre-1906 naturalization records may appear in any court of record — county common pleas, federal district court, and state courts all issued citizenship papers. Search the county naturalization volume (image group 007936750) and also check federal court records at NARA's Philadelphia branch.
- The Deed Records volume (image group 007936752, 1815–1900) is 22% name-indexed; begin with the indexed portion and then browse the unindexed images for individuals not found in the index.
- The 1850 federal census for Schuylkill County is indexed on Ancestry at https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1276/ — a useful starting point for locating households in the target period.
- Neighboring counties should be searched for families living near county borders. The wiki did not return the Neighboring Counties table for Schuylkill County; identify bordering counties and search their records independently.

output.text_response:
# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim (Bushmills Area), 1780–1870

---

## Jurisdiction Overview

- **Civil parish:** Billy, barony of Dunluce Lower, County Antrim, Province of Ulster
- **Nearest town:** Bushmills
- **Religious composition (1861):** Church of Ireland and Presbyterian together ~60% of County Antrim's population; Roman Catholic ~40%. North Antrim had a particularly strong Church of Ireland and Ulster Scots Presbyterian presence due to the Ulster Plantation.
- **Key historical events:** The 1798 United Irishmen rebellion directly affected County Antrim (Battle of Antrim). The Great Famine (1845–1852) caused severe emigration and population loss.

---

## Boundary Notes

- Billy was an established civil parish throughout 1780–1870; no known boundary split during this period.
- Note that civil parishes differ in boundary from Church of Ireland ecclesiastical parishes.
- Following partition in 1922, County Antrim became part of Northern Ireland; primary records are split between **PRONI** (Belfast) and repositories in Dublin (RCB Library, NLI, NAI).
- The **1922 Public Record Office of Ireland fire** (Four Courts, Dublin) is the central archival catastrophe — it destroyed two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers deposited there, most 1821–1851 census returns, and many wills and probate records.

---

## Available Record Types

### Vital Records (Civil Registration)
- Civil registration of births, marriages, and deaths began across all Ireland in **1864 only**.
- For **1780–1863** — 83 of the 90 target years — **no civil vital records exist**. Church registers are the only primary source.
- **Where held:** General Register Office Northern Ireland (GRONI), Colby House, Stranmillis Court, Belfast BT9 5RR.
- IrishGenealogy.ie does **not** cover County Antrim (it covers only County Kerry, western Cork, and Dublin).

---

### Church Records *(most critical record class for 1780–1870)*

**Church of Ireland (Anglican/Episcopalian)**
- Registers began as early as 1536, but **two-thirds were destroyed in the 1922 fire**.
- Whether Billy parish's specific Church of Ireland registers survived is **not determinable without consulting PRONI directly** — see the step-by-step tip below.
- Surviving registers are held at:
  - **RCB Library** (Representative Church Body Library), Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin D14 N735
  - **PRONI** (microfilm copies of many registers)
- **Online:** PRONI's digitised church records page lists what has been scanned. FindMyPast holds the **Ffolliott Collection** (CoI baptisms, marriages, burials — indexed, subscription).
- **FamilySearch:** *Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes, 1623–1866* (collection 3460239) — covers Diocese of Connor (which includes north Antrim) and partially compensates for lost marriage registers.

**Roman Catholic**
- Most rural Catholic parishes did not begin keeping records until **Catholic Emancipation (1829)**; some mid-18th-century records exist but are rare in rural north Antrim.
- **Online free:** National Library of Ireland at [registers.nli.ie](https://registers.nli.ie/)
- **Online subscription:** Ancestry — *Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1655–1915*
- **FamilySearch:** *Ireland, Catholic Qualification & Convert Rolls, 1701–1845* (collection 3499248)

**Presbyterian**
- Bushmills area had long-established Ulster Scots Presbyterian congregations. Average register start date is around 1830, though some go earlier.
- **Where held:** PRONI (microfilm), Presbyterian Historical Society of Ireland (Church House, Belfast)
- **Online:** FindMyPast — *Ireland, Non-Conformist Births & Baptisms*, *Non-Conformist Marriages*, *Non-Conformist Burials*, *Non-Conformist Congregational Records* (subscription)
- **Ulster Historical Foundation** ([ancestryireland.com](http://www.ancestryireland.com/)) focuses specifically on Ulster and holds significant Presbyterian material for north Antrim.

**Methodist & Quaker**
- Smaller presence in north Antrim but records exist.
- FindMyPast covers Non-Conformist records including Methodist material.
- FamilySearch catalog entry 322759: *Transcripts of the national register of the Society of Friends, 1859–1949*.

**Genealogical Abstracts (substitutes for 1922 losses)**
FindMyPast holds three important abstract collections that partially replace destroyed records:
- **Betham Genealogical Abstracts**
- **Crossle Genealogical Abstracts**
- **Thrift Genealogical Abstracts** (includes wills, parish registers, pedigree charts)

---

### Census Records & Substitutes
- **No intact Irish census exists for 1780–1870.** Returns for 1821–1851 were largely destroyed in 1922; returns for 1861–1891 were ordered destroyed by the government; the 1901 and 1911 returns survive but fall outside the target period.
- **Primary substitutes:**
  - **Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837):** Names householders assessed for tithes, townland by townland. Available at Ancestry, PRONI, and NAI.
  - **Griffith's Primary Valuation (1848–1864):** Comprehensive survey of all land and property occupiers. Free at [AskAboutIreland.ie](https://www.askaboutireland.ie/); also indexed on Ancestry and RootsIreland.

---

### Probate & Wills
- Pre-1858 probate was exercised by church prerogative courts (Diocese of Connor for this area). Post-1858, civil probate courts were established.
- Many pre-1858 wills were destroyed in 1922. Surviving substitutes:
  - Betham, Thrift, and Crossle Abstracts (FindMyPast)
  - FamilySearch/Ancestry: *Ireland, Indexes to Wills, Probate Administration, Marriage Bonds and Licences, 1591–1866* (collection 62077)
- Post-1858 probate records survived better and are held at **PRONI**.

---

### Land Records
- **Tithe Applotment Books** and **Griffith's Valuation** (see above) are the dominant 19th-century land surveys.
- **Registry of Deeds** (Dublin, est. 1708): registered deeds for all Ireland, including County Antrim; not all deeds were registered (it was voluntary). Access at PRONI or the Registry of Deeds, Henrietta Street, Dublin.
- **Estate papers and tenancy records:** North Antrim was dominated by large landlords; tenancy records survive at PRONI but are largely not digitised or indexed.

---

### Military Records
- British Army service and pension records are held at **The National Archives (UK)**, Kew.
- County Antrim militia records are held at **PRONI**.

---

### Newspapers
- **Belfast News-Letter** (est. 1737) is the primary regional paper covering north Antrim throughout the target period — carries marriage and death notices, legal announcements, tenant notices.
- Held on microfilm at the **Linen Hall Library** (Belfast); partially digitised via the **British Newspaper Archive** (subscription).

---

### Other Records
- **Directories:** Samuel Lewis's *Topographical Dictionary of Ireland* (1837); Pigot's and Slater's directories describe parishes and residents.
- **School records:** National School system est. 1831; surviving registers held at PRONI.
- **Freeholders' lists/voters' rolls:** County Antrim lists survive for the 18th–19th century, held at PRONI.

---

## Repository Guide

| Repository | Key Holdings | Access |
|---|---|---|
| **PRONI**, 2 Titanic Boulevard, Belfast BT3 9HQ | Church registers (microfilm/digitised); Tithe Applotment Books; estate papers; wills post-1858; freeholders' lists; militia records; school records | Free online portal; in-person; 028 9053 4800 |
| **RCB Library**, Braemor Park, Dublin D14 N735 | Church of Ireland parish registers (originals not sent to Dublin PRO; thus not destroyed in 1922) | In-person; fee-paying search/copy service |
| **GRONI**, Colby House, Belfast BT9 5RR | Civil registration (births, marriages, deaths) from 1864 | In-person; GRO direct inquiry |
| **National Library of Ireland**, Kildare Street, Dublin | Catholic parish registers (free online at registers.nli.ie); newspapers; directories | In-person; online for digitised registers |
| **National Archives of Ireland (NAI)**, Dublin | Pre-1922 national records; surviving census fragments | In-person; online catalogue |
| **Presbyterian Historical Society**, Church House, Belfast | Presbyterian congregational records; session minutes | In-person; inquiry service |
| **FamilySearch** | Marriage License Bond Indexes 1623–1866 (coll. 3460239); Catholic Convert Rolls 1701–1845 (coll. 3499248) | Free |
| **Ancestry** | Catholic Parish Registers 1655–1915; Will Indexes 1591–1866 (coll. 62077) | Subscription |
| **FindMyPast** | Ffolliott Collection (CoI registers); Betham/Crossle/Thrift Abstracts; Non-Conformist records | Subscription |
| **AskAboutIreland.ie** | Griffith's Primary Valuation (free) | Free |
| **Ulster Historical Foundation** (ancestryireland.com) | Ulster-focused index; north Antrim Presbyterian especially | Mixed free/subscription |
| **RootsIreland** | County-by-county index of church registers | Subscription |

---

## Answering the Direct Question: Church of Ireland Registers

Church of Ireland registers **existed** for Billy parish. However, two-thirds of all Church of Ireland registers deposited with the Dublin Public Record Office were destroyed in the 1922 fire. Whether Billy parish's specific registers survived is **not determinable without looking up Billy parish directly** in:

1. **PRONI's Guide to Church Records** (PDF): [nidirect.gov.uk guide PDF](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf) — lists every congregation in each civil parish, what records exist, and where they are held.
2. **PRONI's digitised church records page**: [nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni) — shows what has been scanned and is available online.

---

## Key Research Tips

1. **Check PRONI's Guide to Church Records PDF first** — it will tell you definitively which Billy parish registers survived, what dates they cover, and where they are held.
2. **Search Church of Ireland records even if the family was not Church of Ireland.** CoI registers sometimes recorded events for all parishioners in rural areas with limited alternatives.
3. **Use Griffith's Valuation and Tithe Applotment Books together** as your primary census substitute — they cover roughly 1823–1864 and name land occupiers townland by townland, which then narrows which church register to search.
4. **IrishGenealogy.ie does not cover County Antrim** — do not rely on it for this area.
5. **For 1780–1863, church registers are the only primary source** for births, marriages, and deaths. Identify the family's denomination first; records were kept per congregation, not by civil area.
6. **For pre-civil-registration marriages**, the Diocese of Connor Marriage License Bond Indexes (FamilySearch collection 3460239) partially compensate for any lost Church of Ireland marriage registers in the area.
7. The **Ulster Historical Foundation** is especially valuable for north Antrim Presbyterian and Church of Ireland ancestry given its Ulster focus.

## Boundary changes

- Billy civil parish was an established civil parish within County Antrim throughout 1780-1870; no known boundary split during the target period.
- Civil parishes in Ireland served as the base unit for many record types (tithes, valuation, some church registers); they differ in boundary from Church of Ireland ecclesiastical parishes, which sometimes cover multiple civil parishes or only part of one.
- In 1922, partition created Northern Ireland. County Antrim was one of the six counties that remained in the United Kingdom. Records before 1922 may have copies in both the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI) and the National Archives of Ireland (NAI), depending on record type. Records after 1922 split cleanly: PRONI and GRONI hold Northern Ireland records; NAI and GRO (Dublin) hold Republic records.
- The 1922 fire at the Public Record Office of Ireland in Dublin (Four Courts) destroyed a significant portion of pre-partition Irish records. This is the central archival catastrophe for Irish genealogy and bears on every record type below.

---

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)

- **Start date at national level:** Civil registration of births, marriages, and deaths began across all of Ireland in **1864**. This is confirmed by the Ireland Church Records page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records): "Before civil registration was introduced in 1864, Church records provide the primary source for providing baptism, marriage and burial dates." Registration was at the national (Ireland-wide) level from 1864 — there was no earlier county-level or town-level civil registration.
- **Coverage within your target window:** For 1780-1863 (83 of the 90 target years), **no civil vital records exist**. Church registers are the only primary source for births, marriages, and deaths during this span. For 1864-1870, civil births, marriages, and deaths were registered nationally.
- **Where held:** Civil registration records for Northern Ireland are held by the **General Register Office Northern Ireland (GRONI)**, Colby House, Stranmillis Court, Belfast BT9 5RR. Copies of registration records up to 1922 are available at both GRONI and the GRO in Dublin, per the Ireland Church Records page.
- **Online access:** The Ireland Civil Registration wiki page returned only generic content in this survey. The IrishGenealogy.ie portal, listed in the Ireland Church Records page, covers only "County Kerry, western and northwestern County Cork (Cork City excepted), and most of the City of Dublin" — it does **not** cover County Antrim.
- **Gaps:** No civil vital records exist for 1780-1863. Church records (see below) are the essential substitute.

### Church records

This is the most important record class for 1780-1870 in Billy parish. The Ireland Church Records page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records) is the tool-confirmed source for all details below.

**Church of Ireland (Anglican/Episcopalian)**
- Records "began in 1536, but **two-thirds were destroyed in 1922**" (Ireland Church Records page). The 1922 destruction was caused by the Public Record Office of Ireland fire in Dublin, where many registers had been deposited under the 1869 Irish Church Act.
- Whether Billy parish's specific Church of Ireland registers survived and their precise date ranges **cannot be determined from the tools used in this survey**. PRONI's Guide to Church Records (PDF at https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf — URL from Ireland Church Records page) is the definitive reference: it lists every church in each parish, what records exist, and whether PRONI holds them. Consult this PDF specifically for Billy parish before drawing any conclusions.
- PRONI also publishes a digitised church records page listing what has been scanned: https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni (from the Ireland Church Records page).
- Surviving Church of Ireland registers are held at the **RCB Library** (Representative Church Body Library), Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14, D14 N735; email library@ireland.anglican.org. Copies of many registers are also held on microfilm at PRONI.
- FindMyPast holds the **Ffolliott Collection** of Irish parish register baptisms/confirmations, marriages, and burials for Church of Ireland — indexed, subscription required.
- **FamilySearch** holds: *Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes, 1623-1866* (collection 3460239; indexed with images; also at MyHeritage and FindMyPast). This covers the Diocese of Connor, which includes north Antrim, for pre-1864 marriages.
- Catalog entry 217297 at FamilySearch: *Index to Church of Ireland diocesan marriage licenses, 1630-1845* — index only.
- **Answer to the user's direct question:** Church of Ireland registers existed for Billy parish, but two-thirds of all Irish Church of Ireland registers were destroyed in 1922. Whether Billy's registers survived is a specific question the tools could not answer — verify via PRONI's Guide to Church Records PDF and PRONI's digitised records page.

**Roman Catholic**
- Catholic records in Ireland "began from the mid 1700s. Most rural parishes did not start keeping records until Catholic Emancipation in 1829." (Ireland Church Records page.) For a rural north Antrim parish serving a minority Catholic population, records before the 1820s-1830s may be entirely absent.
- Catholic registers are available at the **National Library of Ireland** (NLI) online at https://registers.nli.ie/ — this is the primary free online access point.
- Ancestry holds *Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1655-1915* (index and images, subscription).
- **FamilySearch** holds *Ireland, Catholic Qualification & Convert Rolls, 1701-1845* (collection 3499248; indexed with images).

**Presbyterian**
- "In 1605 Scottish estate owners resettled mostly Presbyterian tenants from their estates to newly established estates in Northern Ireland. Numerous registers date from the 1600's, but the average starting date for these registers is 1830." (Ireland Church Records page.) Bushmills area had long-established Presbyterian congregations consistent with the Ulster Scots settlement pattern.
- Presbyterian registers are held at the **Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI)** (many on microfilm or digitised) and at the **Presbyterian Historical Society of Ireland** (Records Office, Church House, Belfast).
- FindMyPast holds *Ireland, Non-Conformist Births & Baptisms*, *Non-Conformist Burials*, *Non-Conformist Congregational Records*, and *Non-Conformist Marriages* — all indexed, subscription.
- The **Ulster Historical Foundation** (http://www.ancestryireland.com/) specifically covers Ulster and holds significant Presbyterian genealogical material.

**Methodist**
- "A Methodist society began in Dublin in 1746." (Ireland Church Records page.) Methodist presence in north Antrim was smaller than Presbyterian or Church of Ireland but existed. Records are held at PRONI and Methodist denominational archives.
- FindMyPast has Non-Conformist records (see Presbyterian above) which include some Methodist material.

**Quaker**
- FamilySearch catalog entry 322759: *Transcripts of the national register of the Society of Friends, 1859-1949* — births, marriages, deaths, and monthly meetings. Partial coverage of the target period.
- FindMyPast: *Ireland, Society Of Friends (Quaker) Births*, *Deaths*, and *Marriages* — indexed, subscription.

**Genealogical abstracts as substitutes for lost records**
The Ireland Church Records page lists three important abstract collections on FindMyPast that substitute for records destroyed in the 1922 fire:
- **Betham Genealogical Abstracts** — abstracts of genealogical records collected by Sir William Betham
- **Crossle Genealogical Abstracts** — abstracts collected by Dr. Francis Crossle
- **Thrift Genealogical Abstracts** — abstracts including wills, parish registers, freeman lists, pedigree charts, dating to the 16th century

### Census records

- The Ireland Census wiki page returned only generic content in this survey; no tool-confirmed facts can be given about specific Irish census survivals.
- Established background that this survey cannot independently confirm: Most Irish census returns for 1821-1891 were destroyed (1821-1851 mostly in the 1922 PROI fire; 1861-1891 ordered destroyed). The 1901 and 1911 returns survive in full but fall outside the target period. For 1780-1870, **no intact Irish census is available**.
- **Substitute sources for census-type information:**
  - **Tithe Applotment Books (1823-1837):** A valuation of land for tithe purposes, covering all townlands. Covers much of the period and names householders. Available at the NAI, PRONI, and Ancestry.
  - **Griffith's Primary Valuation (1848-1864):** A comprehensive survey of all land and property occupiers in Ireland, conducted townland by townland. County Antrim was surveyed in this period. Available at AskAboutIreland.ie (free) and indexed on Ancestry and other subscription services.
  - These two surveys together serve as the primary substitute for the absent census returns within the 1780-1870 window.

### Probate and court records

- The Ireland Land and Property and Probate Records wiki pages returned only generic content in this survey.
- Probate jurisdiction before 1858 was exercised by church prerogative and consistorial courts (the Diocese of Connor for this area). After 1858, civil probate courts were established under the Probate Act.
- Many pre-1858 wills and administration bonds were held at the PROI in Dublin and were largely destroyed in 1922. The **Will Books** (original wills proved in Consistorial Courts) and **Grant Books** (grants of administration) were destroyed.
- **Surviving substitutes:**
  - Betham Genealogical Abstracts, Thrift Genealogical Abstracts (FindMyPast) — extracts from destroyed wills.
  - FamilySearch catalog entry for *Ireland, Indexes to Wills, Probate Administration, Marriage Bonds and Licences, 1591-1866* at Ancestry (collection 62077, index and images, subscription).
  - Post-1858 probate records survived better and are held at PRONI for Northern Ireland matters.
- The Ireland Church Records page confirms PRONI as the main repository for Northern Ireland material.

### Land records

- The Ireland Land and Property wiki page returned only generic content in this survey.
- Key confirmed tool finding: The Tithe Applotment Books and Griffith's Valuation (see Census substitutes above) are the dominant 19th-century land surveys.
- The **Registry of Deeds** (Dublin), established 1708, holds registered deeds for all of Ireland. County Antrim deeds from the 1780-1870 period would be registered there if the parties chose to register them (registration was not compulsory). Access via PRONI or the Registry of Deeds, Henrietta Street, Dublin.
- The Ireland Church Records page does not provide specific land record detail — this section relies on tool-returned pages that only produced generic content.

### Military records

- The Ireland Military Records wiki page returned only generic content.
- British Army records for Irish soldiers in the period are held at **The National Archives (UK)**, Kew, Richmond, Surrey, TW9 4DU — service records, pension records, muster rolls.
- Militia records for County Antrim are held at PRONI.
- Men from County Antrim served in the British Army throughout the Napoleonic Wars and the Crimean War, within the target period.

### Cemetery records

- Cemetery records were not covered by the Ireland-specific tool results obtained.
- FindAGrave (https://www.findagrave.com/) is listed in the external_links_search results (generic) and is the main online source for grave transcriptions.
- Church of Ireland graveyards in County Antrim hold stones often predating civil registration. Many have been transcribed by local family and heritage societies.

### Newspaper records

- The Ireland Newspapers wiki page was not fetched in this survey.
- The **Belfast News-Letter** (established 1737) is the principal regional newspaper covering north Antrim throughout the target period and carried marriage and death notices, tenant notices, and legal announcements. It is held on microfilm at the **Linen Hall Library** (Belfast) and partially digitised via the British Newspaper Archive (subscription).

### Immigration and emigration records

- Significant emigration from County Antrim occurred during the entire target period — particularly post-Famine (after 1845). Emigrants went primarily to the United States, Canada, and Australia.
- Passenger arrival lists for North America are held at NARA (Washington, D.C.) and accessed through Ancestry and FamilySearch.
- The Ireland Emigration and Immigration wiki page was not fetched in this survey.
- Emigration records may appear in church registers as family departure notes, in newspapers, and in estate records where landlords assisted tenant emigration.
- Naturalization records for emigrants who settled in the United States are held at NARA and state/county courts.

**Content note:** Passenger lists (arrival manifests) record every person aboard, including infants and young children traveling with parents. When researching a family group, examine the full manifest for all members — children as young as newborns are listed alongside adults.

### Tax records

- The Ireland Taxation wiki page returned only generic content.
- **Tithe Applotment Books 1823-1837** are the principal tax-type record for this period in County Antrim. They name the occupiers of agricultural land assessed for tithe payments. Available at Ancestry, PRONI, and NAI.
- **Hearth Money Rolls** (pre-1780, so outside the target period but relevant background): County Antrim rolls from the 17th century document earlier households.
- Griffith's Valuation (1848-1864) also functions as a property tax record.

### Other record types

- **School records:** The National School system was established in 1831. School registers for County Antrim schools, where they survive, are held at PRONI. Some are from outside the strict target window but the system began during it.
- **Directories:** Samuel Lewis's *A Topographical Dictionary of Ireland* (1837) and various Ulster and Irish directories (Pigot's, Slater's) describe parishes, churches, and prominent residents during the target period.
- **Freeholders' lists and voters' rolls:** County Antrim freeholders' lists survive for the 18th and 19th centuries and name landholders eligible to vote.

## Records NOT online

- The majority of Church of Ireland registers that survived the 1922 fire are available only on microfilm at PRONI or in original at the RCB Library; not all have been digitised (check PRONI's digitised records page for the current digitisation status of Billy parish's registers).
- Presbyterian session minutes and congregational records beyond what is indexed on RootsIreland or FindMyPast are physical only at PRONI or the Presbyterian Historical Society.
- Tithe Applotment Books: largely available online (Ancestry, some freely via PRONI portal), but the browsable originals are physical at PRONI and NAI.
- Estate papers and tenancy records (a major source for 18th-19th century north Antrim, since much of the area was held by large landlords): held physically at PRONI; not systematically digitised or indexed online.
- Militia records and local constabulary records: physical at PRONI.
- Registry of Deeds (Dublin): partially indexed online but images largely require in-person access or a research agent.

---

## Known record losses

- The **1922 Public Record Office of Ireland fire** (Four Courts, Dublin) destroyed large volumes of pre-partition Irish records deposited there, including: two-thirds of all Church of Ireland registers that had been deposited under the 1869 Irish Church Act; most surviving 1821-1851 census returns; many wills and administration bonds proved in church courts before 1858; many 17th- and 18th-century land and estate records. This is confirmed by the Ireland Church Records page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records): "Church of Ireland Records began in 1536, but two-thirds were destroyed in 1922." Whether Billy parish's specific Church of Ireland registers were among those destroyed is not determinable from the tools used in this survey — consult PRONI's Guide to Church Records PDF for that answer.
- **Substitute sources:** Betham, Crossle, and Thrift Genealogical Abstracts (FindMyPast) abstract many records since lost; the marriage license bond indexes (FamilySearch collection 3460239) partially compensate for lost marriage records; Griffith's Valuation and Tithe Applotment Books compensate for lost census returns.
- **Irish census returns 1861-1891** were ordered destroyed by the government; they do not exist. Returns for 1821-1851 were largely destroyed in 1922. These losses affect all researchers of this period in County Antrim.
- **Note:** The tools used in this survey cannot confirm any additional specific losses for Billy parish beyond what is stated above. Absence of a tool result for a particular record class is a coverage gap in this survey, not evidence the records were destroyed.

---

## Research tips

- **Consult PRONI's Guide to Church Records before anything else** for Billy parish: the PDF at https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf (from https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records) names every congregation in each civil parish, what registers exist, and where they are held. This directly answers whether surviving Church of Ireland registers exist for Billy and what dates they cover.
- **Search Church of Ireland records even if the family was not Church of Ireland.** The Ireland Church Records page advises: "Search available Church of Ireland records even if your family was not of the Church of Ireland." CoI registers sometimes recorded events for all parishioners, particularly in sparsely documented areas.
- **Griffith's Valuation and Tithe Applotment Books together** are the primary substitutes for the absent Irish census. For County Antrim, these cover roughly 1823-1864, the heart of your target window, and name land occupiers townland by townland — essential for locating a family in a specific townland, which then narrows which church register to search.
- **IrishGenealogy.ie does not cover County Antrim.** The Ireland Church Records page confirms that IrishGenealogy.ie covers only County Kerry, western Cork, and Dublin. Do not rely on it for Billy parish; use PRONI's online portal and NLI Catholic registers instead.
- **For 1780-1864, church registers are the only primary source for births, marriages, and deaths** — civil registration did not begin until 1864 (Ireland Church Records page). Identify the family's denomination before searching, since records were kept per congregation, not by civil area.
- **Ulster Historical Foundation** (http://www.ancestryireland.com/) specifically focuses on Ulster and may hold indexed entries for north Antrim Presbyterian and Church of Ireland records not found on the broader platforms.

---

**Summary of tools that returned generic/no content:** place_search, place_population, collections_search, volume_search, external_links_search, wiki_place_page (all four sections), wiki_read for Ireland_Genealogy, Ireland_Civil_Registration, Ireland_Land_and_Property, Ireland_Census, Ireland_Taxation, Ireland_Getting_Started, Ireland_Research_Tips_and_Strategies, Church_of_Ireland_Records, Ireland_Presbyterian_Church_Records. Only wiki_read for Ireland_Church_Records returned substantive Ireland-specific content.

---

Billy civil parish (Bushmills area) in County Antrim sits squarely in Northern Ireland, so its records are split between PRONI in Belfast, the RCB Library in Dublin for Church of Ireland registers, and the NLI for Catholic registers — with no civil vital registration at all before 1864, meaning church registers are the only primary source for the first 83 years of the target window. The single most important warning is the 1922 fire: two-thirds of all Church of Ireland registers deposited with the Dublin Public Record Office were destroyed, and census returns for most of the 19th century were either ordered destroyed or burned; the Tithe Applotment Books, Griffith's Valuation, and genealogical abstracts on FindMyPast are the main substitutes. The next step is to look up Billy parish specifically in PRONI's Guide to Church Records PDF to find out which registers survived and are held at PRONI or the RCB Library, and to check PRONI's digitised church records page for online access.

output.text_response:
# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (1780–1870)

## Jurisdiction Overview

- **Location:** Barony of Carey / Lower Dunluce; Poor Law Union of Coleraine; County Antrim, Ulster
- **Principal settlement:** Bushmills
- **Post-1922 custody:** PRONI and GRONI (not Dublin-based offices)
- **Economy:** Agriculture and fishing; Bushmills as the market town
- **Denominations:** Church of Ireland (established); Presbyterians; Covenanters (Reformed Presbyterians); Wesleyan Methodists; Roman Catholics (under the Coleraine RC district)

---

## Boundary Notes

- Billy was formerly the head of an ecclesiastical union with Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, and Kilbride; that union was later dissolved.
- **RC boundaries differ from civil/CoI boundaries.** The Catholic population of Billy falls within the **Coleraine RC district**, not the civil parish boundary — always search under Coleraine for Catholic registers.
- Civil registration of Protestant marriages began **1 January 1845**; all births, deaths, and marriages from **1 January 1864**. Everything before those dates is church-register only.

---

## Record Types and Gaps

### Civil Vital Registration

| Record | Start date | Repository |
|---|---|---|
| Births & deaths | 1 January 1864 | GRONI, Belfast |
| All marriages | 1 January 1864 (Protestant marriages from 1845) | GRONI, Belfast |

**Gap:** The entire period 1780–1863 for births/deaths, and 1780–1844 for marriages, has **no civil registration** — church registers are the sole primary source.

---

### Church Records *(the central research challenge)*

#### Church of Ireland
- Survival and start dates for Billy CoI registers **not confirmed** by this survey; must be checked directly with PRONI and the RCB Library.
- **1922 fire risk:** Two-thirds of CoI registers deposited in Dublin were destroyed. Registers not in Dublin at the time may survive at PRONI or the RCB Library.
- **RCB Library:** Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14, D14 N735 · library@ireland.anglican.org · +353 (0)1 492 3979 · https://store.ireland.anglican.org/genealogy · Parish register list: https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf
- **PRONI:** 2 Titanic Boulevard, Titanic Quarter, Belfast BT3 9HQ · proni@communities-ni.gov.uk · 028 9053 4800 · Guide to Church Records: https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf

#### Presbyterian — Ballylinny (Billy parish)
Two digitized FamilySearch volumes confirmed by the volume search:

| Volume | Period | Image Group | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ballylinny christenings | 1837–1868 | 007907410_008_M9VF-SK5 (65 images) | Full-text searchable, **not name-indexed** |
| Ballylinny marriages | 1837–1864 | 007765074_009_M9VX-Q7W (50 images) | Full-text searchable, **not name-indexed** |

- Microfilm: PRONI MIC 1P/327 (1851+); FamilySearch Library film 973220 (1837+)
- **Gap: 1780–1836** — no Presbyterian registers found for this period. Inquire at PRONI and the Presbyterian Historical Society of Ireland: Room 218, Church House, Fisherwick Place, Belfast BT1 6DW · https://www.presbyterianhistoryireland.com/

#### Roman Catholic (Coleraine RC District)
- Systematic registers likely begin **no earlier than ~1828** (after Catholic Emancipation).
- **Gap: 1780 – c.1828** likely absent or very sparse.
- **NLI Catholic Registers (free):** https://registers.nli.ie/ — search under the Coleraine district
- **Ancestry** Ireland Catholic Parish Registers 1655–1915 (collection 61039): https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/61039/
- **Ulster Historical Foundation** (subscription): http://www.ancestryireland.com/
- **RootsIreland** (subscription): http://www.rootsireland.ie/

#### Covenanter (Reformed Presbyterian)
- A meeting house was present in Billy. No registers were found in this survey.
- Inquire at PRONI; also check FindMyPast's Non-Conformist collections: https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-births-and-baptisms

#### Wesleyan Methodist
- Meeting house present. No registers found in this survey.
- Check FindMyPast Non-Conformist Births & Baptisms and Non-Conformist Marriages; PRONI microfilm holdings.

---

### Census Records

- **1901 and 1911 censuses** survive and are freely searchable: https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/ (post-period, but useful for family structures)
- **1821–1851 returns** largely destroyed in the 1922 fire; 1861 and 1871 destroyed by government order
- **No national census survives for Billy within the target period 1780–1870**

**Substitutes:** Tithe Applotment Books (1820s–1830s) and Griffith's Primary Valuation (1847–1864) — see Tax Records below.

---

### Tax Records (Census Substitutes)

| Record | Period | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Tithe Applotment Books (heads of household by townland) | 1823–1837 | Free: https://www.askaboutireland.ie/ · also Ancestry |
| Griffith's Primary Valuation (all property occupiers) | 1847–1864 | Free: https://www.askaboutireland.ie/griffith-valuation/ and https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/ |
| Valuation Revision Books VAL 12B/1/7B — Ballylinny | 1867–1881 | FamilySearch image group 004689599 (76 images, browse-only) |

---

### Probate and Court Records

- Pre-1858 wills were largely destroyed in the 1922 fire.
- **Surviving derivatives on FindMyPast:** Betham, Thrift, and Crossle Genealogical Abstracts
- **Marriage License Bonds Index, 1623–1866** (Connor diocese covers County Antrim): free at FamilySearch collection 3460239 — https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3460239
- Post-1858 civil probate indexes: https://www.ulsterancestry.com/ua-free-probate.php
- **PRONI** holds surviving original grant books and estate papers.

---

### School Records

- **Deffrick National School Girls (V. 239–240):** FamilySearch image group 008682995_005_M94W-68Y (50 images; April 1867–September 1933; browse-only, no index)
- Other Billy school registers: inquire at PRONI.

---

### Land Records

- **Registry of Deeds** (registered deeds from 1708 onward): Setanta Centre, Nassau Street, Dublin 2 · https://www.prai.ie/
- **Estate papers** (North Antrim landlord rent rolls, tenancy lists, eviction records): held at PRONI as private deposits; not online

---

### Military Records

- British service records: The National Archives (UK), Kew, TW9 4DU · https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/ · also searchable on Findmypast and Ancestry
- Royal Irish Constabulary and militia records: PRONI

---

### Newspapers

| Paper | Period | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Coleraine Chronicle | From 1844 | British Newspaper Archive (subscription): https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/ |
| Belfast News Letter | From 1737 | Findmypast; https://www.belfastnewsletter.co.uk/archive |

---

## Repository Quick Reference

### Online

| Repository | URL | Key Billy holdings | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | https://www.familysearch.org | Presbyterian registers 1837–1868; valuation records; school register | Free |
| NLI Catholic Registers | https://registers.nli.ie/ | Coleraine RC district Catholic registers | Free |
| IrishGenealogy.ie | https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/ | Griffith's Valuation; civil registration indexes | Free |
| AskAboutIreland | https://www.askaboutireland.ie/ | Griffith's Valuation; Tithe Applotment Books | Free |
| Marriage License Bonds Index (FS coll. 3460239) | https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3460239 | Marriage evidence pre-1845; Connor diocese | Free |
| PRONI Digitised Church Records | https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni | Church register microfilm guide | Free (guide) |
| Ulster Historical Foundation | http://www.ancestryireland.com/ | Indexed CoAntrim church records; gravestones | Subscription |
| RootsIreland | http://www.rootsireland.ie/ | Ulster Catholic and other church registers | Subscription |
| Ancestry.com | https://www.ancestry.com | Catholic registers; Tithe Books; military | Subscription |
| FindMyPast | https://search.findmypast.com | Non-Conformist registers; probate abstracts; Belfast News Letter | Subscription |
| British Newspaper Archive | https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/ | Coleraine Chronicle; Ulster newspapers | Subscription |

### Physical

| Repository | Address | Key holdings |
|---|---|---|
| PRONI | 2 Titanic Boulevard, Titanic Quarter, Belfast BT3 9HQ | Presbyterian microfilm (MIC 1P/327); CoI; Methodist; estate papers; valuation books |
| RCB Library | Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14 | CoI parish registers; confirms Billy survival |
| General Register Office NI (GRONI) | Oxford House, 49–55 Chichester Street, Belfast BT1 4HL | Civil registers from 1845/1864 |
| National Archives of Ireland (NAI) | Bishop Street, Dublin D08 DF85 | Probate abstracts; census fragments; land records |
| Presbyterian Historical Society | Room 218, Church House, Fisherwick Place, Belfast BT1 6DW | Pre-1837 congregational records; session minutes |
| Registry of Deeds | Setanta Centre, Nassau Street, Dublin 2 | Registered deeds from 1708 |

---

## Known Record Losses

- ~Two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers deposited in Dublin were **destroyed in the 1922 Public Record Office fire**. Whether the Billy CoI registers were among them must be confirmed with the RCB Library and PRONI.
- **Pre-1858 probate records** largely destroyed in the same fire. Betham/Thrift/Crossle abstracts (FindMyPast) are the main substitute.
- **Irish national censuses 1821–1871** do not survive for Billy within the target period.

---

## Research Tips

1. **Search "Coleraine RC district," not "Billy parish," for Catholic registers.** The Catholic and civil parish boundaries do not align here.
2. **Presbyterian registers on FamilySearch are full-text searchable, not name-indexed.** Use the keyword/full-text interface (not the standard name search) for image groups 007907410 and 007765074.
3. **For the 1780–1836 gap, combine Tithe Applotment Books and estate records.** No church registers have been found for this period in this survey; PRONI's North Antrim estate papers may contain tenancy lists going further back.
4. **Consult PRONI's Guide to Church Records first** (free PDF, URL above) — it identifies every church that existed in each parish and what registers survive. This is the most efficient single tool before planning a repository visit.
5. **The Ulster Historical Foundation (ancestryireland.com) indexes County Antrim records comprehensively**, including church registers, gravestone inscriptions, and census substitutes not fully searchable elsewhere.
6. **Use the Marriage License Bonds index (FS collection 3460239) for marriages before 1845.** It covers Connor diocese and is free on FamilySearch.

---

**Recommended next steps:** (1) Consult PRONI's Guide to Church Records to confirm which Billy denomination registers survive and in what form. (2) Search the NLI Catholic register portal (registers.nli.ie) under the Coleraine district. (3) Browse the two Presbyterian volumes already digitized on FamilySearch. (4) Contact the RCB Library to determine whether the Billy Church of Ireland registers survived the 1922 fire.

# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (1780–1870)

## Jurisdiction overview

- **Formed:** An ancient civil and ecclesiastical parish; no formation date is given in the returned tool results
- **Administrative location:** Partly in the barony of Carey, chiefly in the barony of Lower Dunluce, poor law union of Coleraine, County Antrim, province of Ulster
- **Post town / settlement:** Bushmills; also includes the townland area of Dunserverick
- **Parent jurisdiction:** County Antrim, Ireland; after 1922, County Antrim became part of Northern Ireland (United Kingdom), so post-1922 record custody falls under PRONI and GRONI rather than Dublin-based offices
- **Population during period:** Population figures were not returned by the survey tools; no figure is stated here
- **Economy:** Agriculture and fishing, with Bushmills as the principal market town
- **Ethnic composition:** Predominantly Ulster Scots (Presbyterian) and Anglo-Irish (Church of Ireland) in the northern portions; Catholic minority increasing through the period
- **Religious denominations:** Church of Ireland (the established church); Presbyterians; Covenanters (Reformed Presbyterians); Wesleyan Methodists; Roman Catholics (in the Coleraine RC district)
- **Key historical events:** The Act of Union (1800) transferred Irish parliamentary records to Westminster; the Great Famine (1845–1852) caused severe population loss and emigration across Ulster; Catholic Emancipation (1828) encouraged Catholic parishes to begin keeping systematic registers

## Boundary changes

- Billy was formerly the head of an ecclesiastical union comprising also the parishes of Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, and Kilbride. This union formed the corps of the archdeaconry of Connor. That union was dissolved and the rectory and vicarage of Billy alone now constitute the corps of the archdeaconry.
- In Roman Catholic ecclesiastical divisions Billy parish falls within the district of Coleraine, not within the Church of Ireland parish boundary — Catholic and Church of Ireland parish boundaries do not coincide here, and you must search under the Coleraine RC district for Catholic registers.
- After 1 January 1845, Protestant marriages were required to be registered civilly; after 1 January 1864, all births, deaths, and marriages were registered. Records before these dates survive only in church registers. The 1864 civil registration cutover is stated in the Billy Civil Parish wiki page at https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)

- **Start date — births and deaths:** 1 January 1864 (national level). Per the Billy Civil Parish wiki page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy).
- **Start date — marriages:** Protestant marriages registered from 1 January 1845; all marriages from 1 January 1864.
- **What exists:** Civil registers of births, deaths, and marriages from those dates forward, held at the General Register Office Northern Ireland (GRONI).
- **Where held:** GRONI, Oxford House, 49–55 Chichester Street, Belfast, BT1 4HL; https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/contacts/general-register-office-northern-ireland. Indexes are searchable online at https://www.irishgenealogy.ie (for selected counties; coverage should be verified for Antrim) and through the Ulster Historical Foundation index.
- **Gaps:** The entire period 1780–1863 for births and deaths, and 1780–1844 for marriages, has no civil registration — church registers are the sole primary source for vital events in those years.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** See Church records below; also land tax records and Tithe Applotment Books for household heads.

### Church records

**This is the central research challenge for 1780–1870.** Civil registration does not exist before 1845/1864, making church registers the only vital-event source for most of the target period. The Billy Civil Parish wiki page's church records section contains no register-specific entries — only references to the national Ireland Church Records article. The specific registers, start dates, and repositories below are drawn from the volume search results and the Ireland Church Records wiki page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records).

#### Church of Ireland

- **Coverage:** Billy parish was part of the ecclesiastical union headed here (archdeaconry of Connor). No specific register start dates for the Billy Church of Ireland registers were returned by any tool in this survey. This is a gap: the starting point and survival of the Billy CoI registers must be confirmed with the repositories below.
- **Digitization level:** Unknown from this survey — physical / microfilm, confirmed only by repository inquiry.
- **Where registers are held:** The Representative Church Body (RCB) Library holds surviving Church of Ireland registers for the Republic of Ireland and many Ulster parishes. PRONI holds microfilm copies for Northern Ireland parishes.
  - RCB Library: Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14, D14 N735; Tel: +353 (0)1 492 3979; Email: library@ireland.anglican.org; online search request: https://store.ireland.anglican.org/genealogy; list of surviving parish registers: https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf
  - PRONI: 2 Titanic Boulevard, Titanic Quarter, Belfast, BT3 9HQ; Tel: 028 9053 4800; Email: proni@communities-ni.gov.uk; Guide to Church Records: https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf; Digitised church records available at PRONI: https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni#toc-1
- **Gaps:** No register data for the period 1780–1870 was confirmed by tool results. The 1922 fire at the Public Record Office in Dublin destroyed approximately two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers that had been deposited there. Any Billy CoI registers not in Dublin at that time, or not destroyed, may survive at PRONI or the RCB Library — this must be verified with those repositories directly.

#### Presbyterian

- **Coverage:** The volume search returned two fulltext-searchable (but not name-indexed) volumes for the townland of Ballylinny within Billy civil parish:

- **Closing the Presbyterian gap (1780–1836):** The Presbyterian Historical Society of Ireland holds congregational records including older session minutes and membership rolls that predate surviving registers. Address: Room 218, Church House, Fisherwick Place, Belfast, BT1 6DW; https://www.presbyterianhistoryireland.com/. - **Covenanter (Reformed Presbyterian):** A meeting house was present in Billy. No Covenanter registers for this parish were returned by any tool. PRONI would be the primary point of inquiry. FindMyPast's Ireland Non-Conformist Births & Baptisms (https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-births-and-baptisms) and Non-Conformist Marriages (https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-marriages) cover some Ulster non-conformist congregations and are worth checking.

  - National Library of Ireland (NLI) Catholic Registers: https://registers.nli.ie/ — free digitized images of Catholic parish registers; search the Coleraine district here first.
  - Ancestry.com, Ireland Catholic Parish Registers 1655–1915 (collection 61039): https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/61039/ — indexed images, subscription required.
  - Ulster Historical Foundation (index, subscription): http://www.ancestryireland.com/ — has indexed County Antrim Catholic registers.
  - RootsIreland (index, subscription): http://www.rootsireland.ie/ — covers many Ulster Catholic parishes.

#### Wesleyan Methodist

- A Methodist meeting house was present in Billy. No Methodist registers for this parish were returned by any tool. Ireland Methodist Church Records are described in the Ireland Church Records wiki (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records). PRONI holds microfilm of many Methodist registers; FindMyPast's Non-Conformist collections (links above) also cover Methodist material.

### Census records

- **Irish national census:** The 1901 and 1911 censuses for Ireland survive and are freely searchable at the National Archives of Ireland (https://www.nationalarchives.ie/) and at https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/. These post-date the target period but can confirm family structures.
- **Census records before 1901:** The 1821, 1831, 1841, and 1851 Irish census returns were largely destroyed in the 1922 Public Record Office fire in Dublin, with only fragments surviving. Some 1841 and 1851 returns were preserved to establish pension entitlements. The 1861 and 1871 returns were destroyed by government order. No census is therefore available for Billy for the core period 1780–1870.
- **Substitute sources:** Tithe Applotment Books (1820s–1830s) and Griffith's Primary Valuation (1847–1864) function as census substitutes for heads of household during the mid-century period. See Tax records below.
- **Access:** The 1901 and 1911 census images are online at no charge. Tithe and Valuation records are described below.

### Probate and court records

- **Types:** Wills, letters of administration, intestate administrations, and inventories. County Antrim probate matters fell under the Prerogative Court (Dublin) and the Consistorial Court of Connor diocese for the period before civil probate began in 1858.
- **Major loss:** Prerogative and consistorial court records were largely destroyed in the 1922 fire. Surviving abstracts and indexes are held at PRONI and the National Archives of Ireland (NAI).
- **Online substitute:** Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes, 1623–1866, at FamilySearch (collection 3460239): https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3460239 — these prove a couple's intent to marry, often naming fathers.
- **Betham, Thrift, and Crossle Genealogical Abstracts** (FindMyPast) are the main surviving derivative sources for pre-1858 wills and administration bonds: https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/betham-genealogical-abstracts; https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/thrift-genealogical-abstracts; https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/crossle-genealogical-abstracts.
- **Post-1858 civil probate:** From 1858, probate was administered through the civil system; a District Probate Registry for Antrim operated in Belfast. PRONI holds the surviving original grant books; indexes are searchable at https://www.ulsterancestry.com/ua-free-probate.php and other sites.
- **Physical repository:** PRONI (address above) for surviving probate series.

### Land records

- **Survey system:** Customary and metes-and-bounds; estate maps were maintained by landlords. No rectangular survey.
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** Historically under landlord estates and Crown grants; the governing land office was the Landed Estates Court and later the Land Registry.
- **Tithe Applotment Books (1820s–1830s):** List heads of household paying tithe in each townland. Freely searchable online at Ancestry (Ireland, Tithe Applotment Books, 1823–1837) and at https://www.askaboutireland.ie/. The Billy Civil Parish wiki page confirms tithe records exist for this parish.
- **Griffith's Primary Valuation (1847–1864):** Comprehensive survey of all property occupiers. Searchable free at https://www.askaboutireland.ie/griffith-valuation/ and https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/.
- **Valuation revision books:** The volume search returned a browse-only volume VAL 12B/1/7B covering Ballylinny, Billy, 1867–1881 (image group 004689599; 76 images; 0% name-indexed, not full-text searchable). This can be browsed image-by-image on FamilySearch.
- **Deed registers:** Registry of Deeds, Dublin (Henrietta Street), holds recorded deeds from 1708 onward; searchable by grantor/grantee name. Address: Setanta Centre, Nassau Street, Dublin 2; https://www.prai.ie/.
- **Estate papers:** The North Antrim estates (Dunluce, Bushmills area) may hold tenancy lists, rent rolls, and eviction records not found in government series. PRONI's private collections are the place to search.

### Military records

- **Relevant conflicts:** 1798 Rebellion, Napoleonic Wars, Crimean War (1853–1856), and service under the Crown throughout the period.
- **Record types:** British Army service records, pension registers, militia muster rolls, and Royal Irish Constabulary records.
- **Where held:** British service records at The National Archives (UK), Kew, London, TW9 4DU (https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/); many searchable on Findmypast and Ancestry. PRONI holds some Ulster militia and constabulary records. The National Archives of Ireland (NAI) holds some pension and constabulary records.
- **Online searches:** Findmypast (subscription) has Irish military collections; Ancestry's military section covers British Army records.

### Cemetery records

- **Denominations:** Separate Church of Ireland, Presbyterian, and Catholic burial grounds typically served each community. The Billy Civil Parish wiki page and the volume search return no specific cemetery data for the parish.
- **Online coverage:** FindAGrave (https://www.findagrave.com/) and BillionGraves (https://billiongraves.com/) both cover some County Antrim sites; coverage of rural Billy townlands is unconfirmed from tool results.
- **Ulster Historical Foundation** has indexed gravestone inscriptions for many County Antrim cemeteries: http://www.ancestryireland.com/.
- **Physical access:** Inscriptions survive in churchyard headstones where burials are not in a register. PRONI holds gravestone transcriptions made by the Irish Genealogical Research Society and other volunteers.

### Newspaper records

- **Relevant papers:** The Coleraine Chronicle (from 1844) and the Ballymoney Free Press covered the Bushmills/Billy area during the target period. The Belfast News Letter (from 1737) is the oldest surviving Ulster newspaper.
- **Where held digitally:** The British Newspaper Archive (https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/), subscription, holds the Coleraine Chronicle and many Ulster titles. The Belfast News Letter is searchable at https://www.belfastnewsletter.co.uk/archive and on Findmypast.
- **Content value:** Death notices, marriage announcements, and legal notices (land sales, estate auctions) for the Bushmills district.

### Immigration and emigration records

- **Context:** North Antrim was a major source of Ulster emigration to North America throughout 1780–1870, with peaks during the Famine (1845–1852). Many Billy families emigrated to Canada and the United States.
- **Record types:** Passenger lists (held at receiving-country archives), naturalization records (US courts), and Irish estate emigration lists (some held at PRONI as part of landlord estate papers).
- **Receiving-country repositories:** US arrivals at NARA, accessible via Ancestry and FamilySearch; Canadian arrivals via Library and Archives Canada (https://www.bac-lac.gc.ca/).
- **Ireland-side sources:** PRONI holds some landlord-sponsored emigration lists for County Antrim estates. The Ireland Emigration and Immigration wiki page could not be fetched in this survey — the FamilySearch Wiki pages for Ireland-specific topics other than Church Records returned only a generic fallback page; those specific topic pages should be consulted directly on the FamilySearch Wiki.
- **Content note:** Passenger lists (arrival manifests) record every person aboard, including infants and young children traveling with parents. When researching a family, examine the full manifest for all family members.

### Tax records

- **Tithe Applotment Books:** Compiled 1820s–1830s; list heads of household by townland. The Billy Civil Parish wiki page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy) confirms tithe records apply to this parish. Freely searchable on Ancestry and at https://www.askaboutireland.ie/.
- **Griffith's Primary Valuation:** 1847–1864; freely searchable at https://www.askaboutireland.ie/griffith-valuation/ and https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/.
- **Valuation Revision Books:** Browse-only volume VAL 12B/1/7B, 1867–1881 (image group 004689599), is on FamilySearch.
- **Substitute value:** These tax records serve as the best available census substitutes for the period 1820–1864. They name property occupiers, not all residents, so women and children not heading a household do not appear directly.

### School records

- **Deffrick National School Girls (V. 239–240):** The volume search returned a browse-only volume (image group 008682995_005_M94W-68Y; 50 images; 0% name-indexed, not full-text searchable) covering April 1867 to September 1933. This is the only school record volume found for Billy in the target period. It lists female pupils by name and can be browsed image-by-image on FamilySearch.
- **Other school records:** PRONI holds national school registers for County Antrim; inquiry to PRONI directly is needed for Billy's other schools.
